subject: Spring 2016 State Testing Selection
overview: The School Committee voted to administer PARCC testing for grades 3 through 8 in Spring 2016 and approved a girls hockey program merger with Malden. The committee also reviewed financial reports concerning rising utility costs and approved various salary agreements and a new public information officer position.

items.title: Routine Business
items.summary: Approved the minutes from November 16, 2015, alongside various bills, fund transfers, and payrolls.

items.title: Graduation Date and Gantr Program
items.summary: Approved the June 8, 2016, graduation date for Medford High School and Vocational Technical High School and authorized the continuation of the Gantr program.

items.title: Oral Hygiene Dental Health Program
items.summary: Approved a partnership with local dental associates to provide oral health education and supplies to preschoolers and first graders.

items.title: ImpactAbility Program
items.summary: Approved the implementation of the ImpactAbility Program to teach personal safety and assertive communication skills to students with disabilities.

items.title: Girls Hockey Program Merger
items.summary: Approved a one-year merger of the girls hockey program with Malden to maintain a competitive roster size while sharing user fees and insurance coverage.

items.title: Federal ESEA Renewal Report
items.summary: The superintendent provided an update on the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESEA), which scales back federal oversight and returns authority to states regarding teacher evaluation and school accountability.

items.title: Spring 2016 State Testing Selection
items.summary: Approved the administration of PARCC testing for grades 3 through 8 for Spring 2016 to familiarize students with 'PARCC-like' questions expected in the future MCAS 2.0 version while remaining in a 'held harmless' accountability status.

items.title: Financial Report and Facility Rentals
items.summary: The committee reviewed financial status updates, including a $10,000 annual rent increase for the Japanese Language School and a 22% increase in electricity costs attributed to summer pool operations.

items.title: Snow Protocols and City Infrastructure Updates
items.summary: The committee reviewed school cancellation protocols for inclement weather and received a report from the mayor on safety improvements, including new flashing radar signs and speed bumps near schools.

items.title: Salary Approvals and New Personnel
items.summary: Following an executive session, the committee approved salary agreements for the director of buildings, management parity for principals, lunch attendants, and the creation of a public information officer position.
